newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil strengthen on futures turnaround.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil strengthen on futures turnaround.

text.p: NWE gas oil surged higher on Wednesday as benchmark IPE futures reversed the losses of the past two days, traders said.
The Sept IPE contract rallied in late trade to settle $2.50 higher at $191.75 per tonne, after having traded 25 cents to a $1.00 off for most of the day.
On the cargo market, premiums were firm. Traders said that at least three promptish, 38,000 tonne Russian cargoes had been snapped up at between Sept +75 cents to $1.50, cif NWE.
Low sulphur continued to be a major topic of conversation with a number of French refineries looking for material.
Traders noted, however, that buyers and sellers were distanced with premiums put at Sept +$10.50/+$12.00 for first half September delivery.
"Sellers are holding onto their cargoes. If they can't get at least Sept +$12, they'll wait and offer it over October. Offered premiums over October contract are put at Oct +$15/+$16.
There was talk a German heating oil traded at Sept +3.50, cif Hamburg for first half September delivery. A number of traders said this looked a little low judging premiums closer to Sept +3.50/+4.0.
